news.title: PPMS Real Estates LLP completed the acquisition of additional 14.2% stake in AVI Products India Limited (BSE:523896) from Saroj Kumar Choudhury and Balaji Forex (India) Private Limited.
news.body:
PPMS Real Estates LLP entered into a Share Sale/Purchase Confirmation to acquire an additional 14.2% stake in AVI Products India Limited (BSE:523896) from Saroj Kumar Choudhury and Balaji Forex (India) Private Limited for INR 15.3 million on February 14, 2026. A cash consideration of INR 15.27 million valued at INR 32.5 per share will be paid by PPMS Real Estates LLP. As part of consideration, INR 15.27 million is paid towards common equity of AVI Products India Limited. In related transactions, PPMS Real Estates LLP is acquiring 49.68% stake in AVI Products India Limited through a tender offer and a Share Purchase Agreement. Upon completion of the transactions, PPMS Real Estates LLP will own 88.67% stake in AVI Products India Limited.

news.title: New major risk - Share price stability
news.body: The company's share price has been highly volatile over the past 3 months. It is more volatile than 90% of Indian stocks, typically moving 8.5% a week. This is considered a major risk. Share price volatility increases the risk of potential losses in the short-term as the stock tends to have larger drops in price more frequently than other stocks. It may also indicate the stock is highly sensitive to market conditions or economic conditions rather than being sensitive to its own business performance, which may also be inconsistent. news.title: New major risk - Revenue and earnings growth
news.body: Earnings have declined by 24% per year over the past 5 years. This is considered a major risk. Ultimately, shareholders want to see a good return on their investment and that generally comes from sharing in the company's profits. If profits are declining over an extended period, then in most cases the share price will decline over time unless the company can turn around its fortunes. A trend of falling earnings can be very difficult to turn around. If the company is well already established it may also be a sign the company has matured and is in decline. In addition, if the company pays dividends it will also likely need to reduce or cut them, striking a dual blow to total shareholder returns.
